method: Direct original PNG observations, one open each, before creating any spec or reading any existing modern figure.

subfigures: One shared side-view spherical-mirror frame; no separate panels.

points.label: O
points.fact: Black point at intersection of horizontal principal axis and upward-right secondary axis, left of F.

points.label: F
points.fact: Black point on principal axis between O and P; short vertical focal-plane line passes through it.

points.label: P
points.fact: Vertex on the principal axis at the middle of the curved mirror.

points.label: K
points.fact: Secondary-axis intersection with the mirror, above P.

linesAndCurves.fact: Solid nearly horizontal unarrowed axis extends to both sides; O, F, P lie on it.
Solid unarrowed sloping axis extends below-left of O and above-right of K; O and K lie on it.
One thick continuous mirror curve on the right, concave toward O; right/back side has a bank of short oblique hatch strokes.
Short solid vertical line through F, perpendicular to principal axis; original Chinese label means focal plane.
Sloping unarrowed brace above OK labelled R, from the vicinity of O to K.
Horizontal unarrowed brace between F and P labelled R/2.

relationships: P,K and both mirror endpoints on the sphere centered at O
FP=R/2 in the schematic paraxial model
focal-plane trace through F perpendicular to OP
figures.texturePolicy: Backing hatch bank identifies the nonreflecting side; individual hatch spacing is print texture, not a source scale, grid, or numerical datum.
modernChanges: Regularize scan skew and braces without altering source relations.
Retain approximate/paraxial scope in an explicit label; R/2 is not a universal exact focusing assertion.
Backing hatches are regularized; not represented as counted source data.

subfigures: One vertically mounted optical-disk apparatus; no separate panels.

apparatus.fact: Top central light apparatus: upper clamp/knob, narrow vertical neck and wider lower housing just above disk.
Round front-facing optical disk with thick perimeter and a repeated graduation band; triangular perimeter marks are apparatus graduations, not ray-direction arrows.
Reflector/support region crosses the middle-lower portion of the disk; two thick side fittings are visible.
Long narrow vertical support below disk, ending at a small base.

traces.fact: Three narrow near-vertical illuminated trace bands are visually suggested in the upper central disk, separated by heavy print screening.
Oblique light/reflection traces and the exact reflector contact points cannot be reliably separated from the horizontal screened texture on this single original observation.

figures.directedRays: No independently resolvable drawn ray arrowheads; do not reinterpret perimeter triangles or reflector fittings as arrowheads.
figures.dashedLines: No reliably identifiable intentional dashed construction line; raster interruptions are not evidence of dashed-ray semantics.
exactCountsNotResolved: All reflected traces and contact points
Fine clamp/reflector features occluded by screening
figures.reason: Required source completeness cannot be honestly established. A deterministic apparatus silhouette alone would omit unresolved scientific traces; text context cannot replace independent pixel inventory. No paid artwork or fabricated rays.
figures.scope: The incomplete draft exists only to retain a real native validation failure, not as a renderable or publishable replacement.

points.label: O
points.fact: Black point on principal axis to the left of the ray crossing.

points.label: F
points.fact: Dense common ray-crossing region on axis between O and mirror.

points.label: P
points.fact: Mirror vertex at principal-axis intersection on right.

rayFacts: Seven solid approximately horizontal levels: six off-axis incoming rays and the central shared principal-axis path.
Each of the six off-axis incident rays has a rightward arrowhead before reaching the mirror.
Six solid oblique reflected paths run from the six mirror contact levels toward F and continue to the left.

Reflected arrows point away from the mirror: top mirror contact continues through F toward lower-left, and bottom contact continues through F toward upper-left; paired intermediate paths have the same reversal.
No separate central-ray arrowhead can be resolved on the shared axis; do not add one as an original fact.
Mirror is a continuous concave curve on the right with oblique right-side backing hatches.
figures.focalPlane: Absent from this source; do not import Figure 141 focal-plane trace.
labels: printed 143 caption outside the scientific frame
relationships: O,F,P collinear with F between O and P
All incoming off-axis levels parallel to OP
Each incident endpoint lies on mirror
Each reflected path crosses the schematic F and continues left
All six incident arrows point toward mirror and six reflected arrows away
figures.texturePolicy: Backing hatches and scan skew are nonnumerical print conventions.
modernChanges: Regularize scan skew and spacing; preserve all six off-axis rays and central axis.
Explicit Paraxial approximation and Schematic, not to scale labels; the common F is a model construction, not exact all-aperture spherical focusing.
Regularized hatches and small construction endpoint markers are modern rendering aids, not extra source data.
Do not copy the embedded printed caption into the ray frame.
